## Findings

**Finding 1 — the `compound-head-lost` rule fires without any evidence a head word was lost (production code; the work finding).**
The rule is `keyHeadPhrase.Length >= 2 && parsedNameTokens.Length == 1 && parsedName == keyHeadPhrase[0]`. `KeyHeadPhrase` = all key-description tokens up to the first state token, so for FDC descriptions it includes every post-name qualifier; the condition therefore degenerates to "parsedName is a single token equal to the key's first token" — true for nearly every single-word food name, whether or not anything was dropped.
- **27 of 29** batch `compound-head-lost` rows and **5 of 16** debug rows have no non-first key-head token anywhere in the rawText (python: singularized `keyHead[1:]` ∩ rawText tokens = ∅). Indisputable rows: `Flour` (accepted row **identical** to key row), `1 piece onion` (accepted **identical** to key), `300 g beef` / `180 g beef` (key `Beef, chuck, roast, boneless, choice` vs accepted `Beef, ground, 90% lean` — a row-choice, not a lost head), `1 piece boiled egg` ×6 (key Cooked vs accepted None — the brief's own **state-mismatch** shape), `1 bunch coriander` ×4.
- The converse miss: `1/4 cup chopped water chestnuts` (parsedName `water`, key head `waterchestnut chinese`) is a *genuine* truncated head and is classified `sibling-food`.
- The largest bucket (29/74 = 39 % of batch) is thus mislabeled, and the report's P12.16 re-attribution ("7 = 4 bread-crumb + lemon peel + 2% milk + hard-cooked eggs") is built on the contaminated cell.
- Minimal fix: fire `compound-head-lost` only when some `keyHeadPhrase[1:]` token (singularized) also appears in the normalized rawText tokens — keeps the §2 bread-crumbs line, kills the 27+5 false positives, lets the egg rows fall to `state-mismatch`.

**Experiment:** I did (a) an independent python recount of `auto && !correct` lines in both fresh traces, (b) byte-diffed fresh re-runs of both census commands and the pairs command against all five recorded artifacts, (c) fed a synthesized 6-line trace through the production CLI entry point covering ladder edges (jar unit, can with both rows canned, multi-atom with a non-first accepted atom, missing `actualDataTypes`, unknown atom path, sealed set), (d) a 17-site mutation inventory over the new census code (mutate → `dotnet test` → `git checkout`), and (e) a rawText-evidence audit of every `compound-head-lost` row; I expected the instrument to classify the known-way cases per the brief's ladder and the tests to go red on every mutated decision term; what actually happened: claims 1, 2, 4, 5 held exactly (all diffs byte-identical; guards exit 1 with 0-byte stdout; pairs denominator independently 44), but the synthetic `1 can crushed tomatoes`-shaped row with a non-canned key, the row-choice-tier row, and the missing-tier row **all collapsed into `compound-head-lost`**, and 27/29 batch + 5/16 debug `compound-head-lost` rows show no head word in the rawText at all (including two rows where accepted == key is byte-identical), while the one genuinely truncated head (`water chestnuts` → `water`) landed in `sibling-food`; three mutations (pack-unit key-Canned term, overrideKey paren-fold, `TierRank` order) survived the suite, the last one flipping the report's `key higher` split.

**Commit:** `<sha>` · **Files:** 20 · **Elapsed:** ~260 min (incl. one NO-GO rework round)

## What changed
A new C# CLI instrument, `tools/LetUsCook.AutoWrongCensus` (Generic Host, Replay-shaped), classifies
**every** `auto == true && correct == false` line of a debug or batch trace into exactly one accepted-vs-key
relation (`pack-unit-state`, `compound-head-lost`, `state-mismatch`, `sibling-food`, `row-choice-tier`,
`same-head-other-qualifier`, `no-label`, `other`) and exactly one decision site (`override`, `reuse`,
`ranker`, `curated`), using **only** production helpers — `FdcNormalizer.NormalizeToTokens`,
`FdcMatcher.ExtractCandidateState`/`ExtractCandidateSatisfiers`, `FdcDescriptionParser.Parse(...).HeadTerm`,
`IngredientLineResolver.SingularizeToken` — reached via two `InternalsVisibleTo` entries in
`src/LetUsCook.Fdc/LetUsCook.Fdc.csproj` (the only `src` change). `census <trace.jsonl>` writes the full
TSV (header + one row per auto-wrong line) to stdout and the relation × site matrix, `other` rate,
missing-field counts, `overrideKey` yes/no, the `ShouldReuse(parsedName, linkedIngredientId)=false` count
and per-line qualifier diffs to stderr; it refuses any set other than `debug`|`batch` (D-029) before
writing anything. A second subcommand, `pairs <census.tsv> <trace.jsonl>`, emits the joined
window/`compound|other` table (5 columns) that P12.18 consumes.

One rule was reworked after the first falsifier pass (NO-GO, class `work`): `compound-head-lost` now
requires, beyond the brief's "key's HeadTerm has two or more words, parsedName equals only its first word",
that **at least one token of the head phrase beyond the first word appears in the rawText** (both sides
normalised and singularised). Without it the bucket degenerated into "parsed name is one word and the key
description is wordy" — `2 cups flour` against `Flour, wheat, all-purpose, enriched, bleached` (accepted
row **identical** to the key) classified `compound-head-lost`; 27/29 batch rows of that bucket had zero
head-loss evidence. With the evidence gate: the §2 bread-crumbs line still fires (`crumbs` is in the
rawText), flour/boiled-egg/beef rows fall to their true classes, and a real parse-cut (`1 cup chopped
water chestnuts` → parsed `water` against a `Water, chestnuts, …` key) is caught.

This is an instrument: it removes no error and predicts nothing; it makes the auto-wrong buckets countable.

           acceptedState=None (full row verbatim in Resources/features/f-428/runs/P12.13/autowrong-debug.tsv)
```

`pack-unit-state × reuse` (canned tomatoes), `compound-head-lost × override` (bread crumbs,

## What this change cannot fix
Nothing was fixed; this is the instrument. The census also cannot see *why* the ranker or reuse layer
picked the row it picked — it names the head/state/tier difference only. Design choices the next brief
should know about (per §8):
- The **key head phrase** for `compound-head-lost` is the normalised tokens up to the first token for
  which production state/satisfier extraction is non-empty, each singularised by production
  `SingularizeToken`. `FdcLexicon.ModifierWords` is deliberately **not** a stop condition — `crumb` is
  in that lexicon and stopping there would reduce the §2 bread-crumb head to one word.
- The head phrase alone is a property of the key description, not of the line: the rule therefore also
  requires head-tail evidence in the rawText (the NO-GO-1 fix above). A parse-cut where the *rawText*
  carries the tail but the key's head is a single token (the cup-unit water-chestnut line) is not
  `compound-head-lost` under the brief's definition; it lands in `sibling-food`.

  text-mangles rather than calls, because it is private in `FdcMatcher`; the fold is
  `rawText[..IndexOf('(')]` trimmed and lowered, matched against the embedded `exact-overrides.json`
  keys.
- The brief §5 invocation is positional (`pairs <census.tsv> <trace>`); its §4 `--pairs` flag wording
  is superseded by the §5 command form.
